name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 342 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 20% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 342 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 20 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: LG Manoj Sinha chaired a high-level security meeting in Kashmir and reviewed the security situation and winter preparedness. Sakina Itoo flagged hardships caused by security convoys on the national highway. Chhattisgarh will downgrade the security cover of 116 Bastar leaders as Maoist violence declines. An ISI-backed Kashmir Study Group is shifting its terror strategy to south India amid intensified security in the north. 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: LG Manoj Sinha ledet et høyt nivå sikkerhetsmøte i Kashmir og gjennomgikk sikkerhetssituasjonen og vinterberedskapen. Sakina Itoo påpekte vanskeligheter forårsaket av sikkerhetskonvoier på nasjonalveien. Chhattisgarh vil nedgradere sikkerhetsdekningen for 116 ledere i Bastar ettersom maoistisk vold avtar. En ISI-støttet Kashmir Study Group skifter terrorstrategi til Sør-India etter intensivering av sikkerheten i nord. 437 dødsfall i kamp ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
